title: Decision Tree Primitive
description: Structured decision tracking for grill-mode sessions. A tree of Decision nodes, each with status, dependencies, and the standard branch taxonomy.

branchTaxonomy.description: Standard branches every decision tree must cover. New branches may be added via CreateBranch if the subject demands one not in this set.

branches.question: What changes for the user? What is success?
What is explicitly in scope, out of scope, deferred?
What are the performance, security, deadline, budget, and compatibility constraints?
What are the components, boundaries, data flow, and entity cardinality?
What breaks? What are the partial failure, retry, rollback, and observability strategies?
What proves correctness? What is the first failing test?
How does this ship without breaking prod?
What does back-out look like if it goes wrong?

status.description: resolved: answer is known. deferred: will decide when trigger condition is met. out_of_scope: explicitly not in this design.

answer.description: Concrete answer. Required if status is resolved. Must be the deferred trigger condition if status is deferred.

dependsOn.description: IDs of decisions that must be resolved before this one.

alternatives.description: Alternatives considered and rejected. Required for resolved decisions.

traversalRules.depthFirst: Resolve all decisions in one branch before moving to the next.
traversalRules.dependencyOrder: If decision A depends on B, resolve B first. Surface this constraint explicitly.
traversalRules.noHandwaves: Status must be resolved, deferred with a concrete trigger, or out_of_scope. No 'probably', no 'we'll figure it out later'.

conditions: Every standard branch has at least one decision (resolved, deferred, or out_of_scope)
Every deferred decision has a concrete trigger condition
Agent can write the full spec from the resolved decisions alone

storageTarget: Session artifact — may be written to .specify/specs/<NAME>/decisions.json or emitted inline.
